plan: My value is $48. I need to consider how the other bidders, Betty and Charles, might bid. A common strategy is to bid one's value. If they do that, and I bid slightly higher, I win but make very little profit. If I bid lower, I risk losing. A reasonable strategy is to bid slightly below my value to ensure a profit if I win, but not so low that I'm likely to lose. I will bid $47.5.

I will start with a baseline strategy of bidding a fraction of my value, say 80%. This would be 38 * 0.8 = 30.4. I expect the other bidders to also bid a fraction of their value. If I bid slightly above their expected bid, I might win but pay too much. If I bid lower, I will likely lose. I will bid $30.4.

My value is $12. I want to maximize my profit. I should bid less than my value to ensure a profit if I win. If others bid close to their values, I should bid lower. If others bid randomly, I should bid a bit higher to increase my chances of winning while still maintaining a profit. A reasonable starting bid is slightly below my value, say $11.5. I will bid $11.5.
